geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the bent dominant mass with a courtyard logic so the primary access edge can become a legible public threshold.
Create a sufficiently sized void to read as usable public space rather than a decorative cut.
Align the opening with the verified access side in the program frame.
Make the courtyard-conditioned mass the new dominant geometry while preserving the existing bent bar ancestry.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the primary bar into a courtyard-capable massing rule so the ground edge can become legibly public instead of sealed.
Keep the dominant bar orientation stable while changing its spatial logic to support an access-aligned void.
Open the carved/public side toward the program-frame access side so the street threshold becomes explicit.
Set a bounded courtyard margin large enough to register as usable public space without fragmenting the mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant compact mass with a coherent bent/cantilever gesture across views, so it clears the basic massing coherence gate and does not appear view-dependent or self-colliding. The silhouette is legible but somewhat generic and boxy in section, with only modest continuity of the bend. Programmatically it is plausible for neighborhood living/mixed-use because there is a clear main body and an upper hierarchy, but the public threshold is weak: the verified road frontage edge is answered more by a sealed flank than by a legible ground court, undercut, or entry seam. The carved void is present but too small and not convincingly public. Overall, this is a viable early massing with repair integrity, but it needs a stronger access-aligned void and ground response to better satisfy the semantic brief.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked-but-coherent mixed-use massing with a legible lower datum and compact upper body.
